editorial:
Imagine being dropped into a gritty world where tension runs high and the stakes feel real. You follow a man named Ishimatsu who is caught up in a cycle of anger and conflict. The movie feels like a slow burn that builds up to a breaking point, making you feel the pressure he is under. It has that classic black-and-white look that makes the city feel cold and lonely, which fits perfectly with the mood of the story. You will find yourself wondering if he can actually find a way out of his mess or if he is just doomed to keep fighting.

The acting is top-notch and makes the characters feel like real people rather than movie tropes. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the payoff in the end makes it worth the wait. If you love old-school crime dramas, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Ishimatsu finally faces the people he has been fighting. Instead of a happy ending, the movie shows that violence only leads to more pain. He realizes that his anger has pushed everyone away. The final scenes show him broken and alone, proving that you cannot fight your way to a better life. It ends on a sad note that makes you think about the choices he made.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Japanese crime stories and character studies.
